description: The provided grouped bar chart illustrates the number of datasets over time, categorized by the number of languages they contain. The horizontal category axis is labeled "Year" and displays a sequential, chronological range of years from 2012 to 2022. The vertical value axis, labeled "Number of datasets," employs a logarithmic scale with numeric tick labels at 10¹ (10) and 10² (100), supplemented by horizontal grid lines. Within each year on the horizontal axis, the bars are grouped side-by-side according to a legend titled "Languages," where blue bars represent datasets with "1" language (positioned on the left of each group) and orange bars represent datasets with "2+" languages (positioned on the right). From 2012 to 2016, only datasets with "1" language are depicted, starting with the shortest bars at approximately 2 datasets in 2012 and 2013, and growing to roughly 12 by 2016. Datasets with "2+" languages first appear in 2017 with a value of approximately 5, alongside a blue bar indicating roughly 20 datasets. The highest recorded value for "1" language datasets occurs in 2021, with the tallest overall bar reaching approximately 150 datasets, paired with an orange bar indicating 10 datasets. The tallest orange bar appears in 2020, corresponding to roughly 20 datasets alongside 100 datasets for the "1" language category. The bars for the final year, 2022, are visually emphasized through a faded, lighter opacity for both the blue (roughly 30 datasets) and orange (roughly 2 datasets) bars.
